beats.text: Deep in the forest, they visited the ashram of Sage Atri, one of the seven great sages of the universe.
Atri welcomed them like his own children, and led Sita to meet his wife.
Anasuya was very old, her hair white, her body thin from penance. Once, her prayers had made the Ganga flow through a land dying of drought, and had stopped ten years of famine.
Atri's wife, Anasuya, a woman of great virtue, embraced Sita like a daughter.
She was so pleased with Sita's devotion to Rama that she gave her divine gifts: a garland that never withers, clothes that never fade, and an ointment that would keep her beautiful forever.
She spoke to Sita about devotion and strength, wisdom Sita would need in the days ahead.
The next morning, the three walked on into the Dandaka forest, wearing those gifts.
